pull.title: test, refactor: extract script template helpers and expand sigop coverage
pull.body:
**Problem:** Sigop counting lacks focused coverage for malformed `PUSHDATA` encodings and common script templates.
`CScript::GetSigOpCount` is also overloaded for direct script counting and P2SH redeemScript counting.
Several call sites repeat byte-level template checks, while `MAX_OPCODE` and `HasValidOps()` do not make their pre-Taproot scope clear.
Existing block benchmarks measure deserialization and validation, but not legacy sigop counting.

**Fix:** Add focused unit and fuzz coverage for sigop counts, malformed push encodings, common script templates, and opcode validity.
Rename the `bool` overload to `CountSigOps` and replace the `scriptSig` overload with the standalone `CountP2SHSigOps` helper.
Centralize script template sizes and extract cheap inline predicates for common templates.
Rename `MAX_OPCODE` and `HasValidOps()` to `MAX_BASE_OPCODE` and `HasValidBaseOps()` to make their scope explicit.
Add a separate `SigOpsBlock` benchmark.

**Follow-up:** The optimization in [#32532](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32532) can reuse these predicates instead of repeating byte checks ([d76d753](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/d76d7531dfcc7ef2d104b8977a2239cb1fc89119)).

Rebased, simplified PR description, dropped a low-value `script_ops` fuzz call for a fixed non-`P2SH` case already covered by unit tests, and added better fuzz coverage by passing a separate fuzzed `script_sig` to `CountP2SHSigOps(script_sig, script)`.

I also reused `uint160::size()` / `uint256::size()` for the script size constants, switched the `P2A` test to the existing `PayToAnchor` / `ANCHOR_BYTES` helpers, and added #35218-style assertions to fuzz targets that construct standard script templates.

Differences since previous review (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32729#pullrequestreview-3680924174):

* Dropped 0cf8b8fb72a0efc5bbac1b4faa917d0eae1ccc5d since similar changes have been done through other PRs.

Code review ACK f51e4a6abb28403d3ff28c9bc5d55aa851c3bb62. Lots of nice changes here. Increased test coverage might be the biggest practical benefit but I think the change getting rid of `GetSigOpCount` overloading and having dedicated `CountSigOps`, `CountP2SHSigOps` and `CountWitnessSigOps` functions is a major readability improvement that makes the code a lot less confusing.

Left various suggestions below but none are important

Thanks again for the reviews! I pushed an empty rebase first to simplify range-diffs (which are usually difficult when commits are merged and split). In the last push, I reorganized the stack so the sigop characterization tests precede the API refactors.
I split the old combined test commit into separate sigop and opcode-name commits, split the P2SH refactor into helper extraction and caller migration, and merged the standalone `OP_CHECKSIGADD` test into the base-opcode rename.
Template fuzz assertions now live with the helper commits they exercise instead of a separate batch commit.

I also applied the review suggestions around benchmark naming, `CountP2SHSigOps` argument clarity, independent fuzz inputs, bidirectional template checks, and additional sigop edge cases.
The commit messages now match these boundaries and explain the base-script opcode scope.

Production code derives shared sizes and indexes from the existing hash and `CPubKey` constants, while tests and fuzzers deliberately keep redundant literals as independent format checks.

Old behavior:
1. `txin.scriptSig.GetSigOpCount(/*fAccurate=*/true)` would count `txin.scriptSig` sigops.

```c++
/**
 * Count the number of signature operations (sigops) in this script.

 * The `fAccurate` parameter controls how `CHECKMULTISIG` operations are counted.
 * When enforcing the `MAX_BLOCK_SIGOPS_COST` limit, set `fAccurate` to `true` when

 * the redeemScript/witnessScript began to be counted precisely, using the
 * preceding OP_N to determine the number of pubkeys.
 */
unsigned int CountSigOps(bool fAccurate) const;
```
